tasks.behavior: The agent skill teaches every diagram kind it claims to support, with a worked example of each that validates, lays out and exports; and the repository reads like an open-source project, with a README that says what Mapgrain is and how to start, a contributing guide, a code of conduct, a real security policy, and issue and pull request templates.
acceptance: The skill ships a worked example of every diagram kind, and every example validates, builds a scene and exports HTML.
The schema reference names every node kind and edge type each diagram kind accepts, and a test fails if the two ever drift.
The skill names the failure modes an agent actually hits, including the decision-outcome rule and the id pattern.
The README states what Mapgrain is, how to start in a minute, the five kinds, the CLI, the agent skill, and where the feature status lives, keeping every media link.
CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and a root SECURITY.md disclosure policy exist, and issue and pull request templates are in place.
The feature and capability tables name what the last two slices shipped.
The README media is recaptured from the current build.
